enriched_description: Medium-sized quadrupedal mammal with a compact, well-proportioned body structure. The coat is profusely double-layered: a soft woolly undercoat beneath a long, straight to slightly wavy outer coat that hangs in dense strands, typically in white, cream, gold, tricolor, or smoky gray. The face is heavily furnished with hair forming a distinctive fall over the eyes and a beard around the muzzle, obscuring facial features. Ears are pendant-shaped, hanging close to the head, covered in long feathering. The tail is carried curled over the back in a tight spiral, heavily plumed with long hair creating a fan-like appearance. Legs are heavily feathered with hair extending to the paws, giving a columnar appearance. The overall silhouette resembles a miniature Old English Sheepdog with a shaggy, unkempt profile. Paw pads are large and well-furred, an adaptation to cold Tibetan terrain. Body length slightly exceeds height at withers. The gait is springy and agile despite the heavy coat.

Small toy-sized quadrupedal mammal with a fine-boned, elongated rectangular body structure. The defining feature is the floor-length, pin-straight coat with a distinctive blue-and-tan coloration: rich steel blue covering the body from occiput to tail base, with tan markings on the head, chest, and legs. The coat texture is exceptionally silky and lustrous, resembling human hair, with no undercoat. The hair parts naturally along the spine, creating a clean center parting. The head is small and wedge-shaped with a moderately long muzzle. Ears are small, V-shaped, and erect, positioned high on the skull. The tail is docked or naturally carried high, plumed but not heavily feathered. Eyes are small, dark, and almond-shaped, set beneath a silky topknot that falls forward. The body is low to the ground with short, fine-boned legs. Overall proportions emphasize length over height, creating a sleek, streamlined profile. The coat requires visual distinction from the similar Yorkshire Terrier by its larger size and more substantial bone structure.

Medium-sized quadrupedal mammal with a square-proportioned, well-balanced body structure. The entire coat is a uniform pale wheaten color ranging from light beige to golden honey, with no other colors permitted. The coat texture is soft, silky, and gently wavy, falling in loose waves rather than tight curls. A distinctive feature is the abundant facial furnishings: a full beard and mustache that obscure the lower face, and a prominent fall of hair over the eyes giving a shaggy, veiled appearance. The head is rectangular in profile with a flat skull and moderate stop. Ears are V-shaped, medium-sized, folding forward close to the cheeks. The tail is typically docked and carried erect, covered in the same wavy coat. Legs are moderately feathered with hair extending to the pasterns. The body is compact with a level topline and deep chest. Proportions are nearly square, with body length approximately equal to height at withers. The coat has a characteristic 'falling' quality, draping naturally rather than standing away from the body. Puppies are born darker and lighten to the wheaten shade with age.

Small, compact quadrupedal mammal with a sturdy, well-balanced body structure. The coat is exclusively pure white, double-layered with a harsh, straight outer coat approximately 5 cm in length and a soft, dense undercoat providing insulation. The outer coat stands away from the body, creating a crisp, weather-resistant profile. The head is round and domed with a short, strong muzzle tapering to a black nose. Ears are small, pointed, and carried erect, positioned wide apart on the skull, giving an alert, fox-like expression. Eyes are dark, widely set, and deep-set beneath prominent brow ridges. The tail is short (13-15 cm), thick at the base, tapering to a point, carried erect and never curled over the back. Legs are short, muscular, and heavily boned relative to body size, with dark pigmented skin and black nails. The body is compact with a level topline and deep chest. The overall silhouette is terrier-typical: low-slung, sturdy, and alert. The white coat provides high contrast against natural backgrounds, and the erect ears and tail create a distinctive triangular profile when viewed from the side.

Small, compact quadrupedal mammal with a slightly elongated body structure. The defining feature is the profuse, heavy, floor-length coat that is straight, hard in texture, and dense, parting naturally along the spine. Coat colors include golden, sandy, honey, dark grizzle, slate, smoke, parti-color, white, and black. The coat drapes heavily, creating a sweeping, flowing silhouette that obscures the body outline. The head is heavily furnished with a prominent topknot falling forward over the eyes and a full beard and mustache that obscure the muzzle. Eyes are medium-sized, dark brown, and oval-shaped, partially hidden beneath the fall. Ears are pendant-shaped, hanging close to the head, heavily feathered and blending into the neck coat. The tail is heavily plumed, carried curled over the back in a characteristic 'chrysanthemum' shape where the hair radiates outward from the tail base. Legs are heavily feathered with hair extending to the paws, creating a cylindrical appearance. The body is longer than tall with a level topline. The overall profile is that of a heavily coated, low-slung dog with a distinctive flowing gait. The coat requires visual distinction from the Tibetan Terrier by its heavier, straighter texture and more pronounced facial furnishings.

Medium to large-sized quadrupedal mammal with an athletic, streamlined body structure optimized for swimming and retrieving. The coat is dense, fine to medium in texture, flat-lying against the body with moderate feathering on the chest, legs, and tail. Coat colors are solid black or solid liver (dark brown), with a glossy, water-resistant sheen. The head is clean-cut with a flat skull and moderate stop, featuring a long, powerful muzzle with a scissors bite. Eyes are medium-sized, brown to dark brown, almond-shaped, conveying an intelligent, keen expression. Ears are small to medium, pendant-shaped, lying close to the head, set level with the skull. The tail is straight, carried level with the topline or slightly above, with moderate feathering creating a flag-like appearance. The body is long and low with a deep chest reaching to the elbows, a level topline, and well-sprung ribs. Legs are long, muscular, and straight-boned with well-arched feet and thick pads. The overall silhouette is elegant and racy, resembling a leaner, flatter-coated Golden Retriever. Proportions emphasize length over height, with a characteristic otter-like tail. The gait is smooth, efficient, and ground-covering with minimal vertical oscillation.

Large, powerful quadrupedal mammal with a square-proportioned, athletic body structure. The defining feature is the coat composed entirely of tight, crisp curls covering the entire body from head to tail, with no feathering on the legs, ears, or tail. Coat colors are solid black or solid liver (dark brown). The curls are small, uniform, and stand away from the body, creating a distinctive textured, almost woolly appearance. The head is wedge-shaped with a flat skull and a long, deep muzzle. Eyes are large, oval-shaped, and dark, set obliquely with a keen, intelligent expression. Ears are small, pendant-shaped, lying close to the head, covered in short curls. The tail is moderate in length, thick at the base, tapering to a point, carried nearly level with the back, covered in short curls. The body is deep-chested with a short, strong loin and well-sprung ribs. Legs are long, straight-boned, and muscular with well-arched, cat-like feet. The overall silhouette is tall, square, and imposing with a distinctive curly-textured profile. The coat provides visual distinction from all other retriever breeds by its complete lack of feathering and uniform curl pattern. The gait is smooth, powerful, and effortless with a characteristic springy stride.

Medium to large-sized quadrupedal mammal with a well-balanced, powerful body structure. The coat is dense, water-repellent, with a flat or wavy outer coat and a soft undercoat. Coat colors range from rich lustrous golden to light cream, with feathering on the back of the forelegs, underside of the body, front of the neck, and back of the thighs. The tail is thick and muscular at the base, carried with a merry action, covered in long feathering creating a flag-like appearance. The head is broad with a straight profile, a well-defined stop, and a deep, wide muzzle. Eyes are dark brown, widely set, with a friendly, intelligent expression. Ears are medium-sized, pendant-shaped, hanging close to the cheeks. The body is slightly longer than tall with a level topline, deep chest, and well-sprung ribs. Legs are muscular with substantial bone, straight forelegs, and well-arched feet with thick pads. The overall silhouette is symmetrical, balanced, and powerful with a characteristic golden-hued, feathered profile. The coat has a distinctive lustrous sheen in sunlight. Proportions are harmonious with no exaggerated features. The gait is smooth, powerful, well-coordinated, with good reach and drive.

Medium to large-sized quadrupedal mammal with a sturdy, athletic, well-balanced body structure. The coat is short, dense, and straight with a hard, weather-resistant texture and a soft undercoat. Coat colors are solid black, solid yellow (ranging from fox-red to light cream), or solid chocolate brown. The coat lacks feathering on the legs, body, or tail, creating a clean, sleek profile. The head is broad with a clean-cut skull, moderate stop, and a medium-length, powerful muzzle. Eyes are medium-sized, brown or hazel, conveying an intelligent, kindly expression. Ears are medium-sized, pendant-shaped, hanging close to the head, set slightly back. The defining feature is the 'otter tail': thick at the base, gradually tapering toward the tip, medium length, covered in short, dense hair creating a rounded, otter-like appearance. The body is slightly longer than tall with a deep chest, level topline, and well-sprung ribs. Legs are straight-boned, muscular, with compact, well-arched feet and thick pads. The overall silhouette is clean, athletic, and powerful with no feathering or long hair. The gait is free, effortless, and ground-covering with minimal vertical oscillation.

Medium to large-sized quadrupedal mammal with a powerful, well-balanced body structure optimized for cold-water retrieving. The defining feature is the unique double coat: a short, harsh, wavy outer coat with a dense, fine, woolly undercoat that is oily and water-repellent. The coat has a distinctive deadgrass, sedge, or brown coloration ranging from deep brown to light tan, often with a grizzled or brindled appearance. The texture is greasy to the touch with a characteristic musky odor. The head is broad and round with a medium-length muzzle and a slight stop. Eyes are yellowish or amber-colored, medium-sized, conveying an intelligent, intense expression. Ears are small, pendant-shaped, hanging close to the head, set high on the skull. The tail is medium length, thick at the base, tapering to a point, carried straight or with a slight curve, covered in short wavy hair. The body is slightly longer than tall with a deep chest, level topline, and well-sprung ribs. Legs are long, muscular, with well-arched feet featuring webbed toes for swimming. The overall silhouette is powerful and substantial with a distinctive wavy, deadgrass-colored profile. The coat provides exceptional insulation in icy water. The gait is smooth, efficient, and powerful with a characteristic rolling motion.
